# Receiver syntax boundary probes

Copyright 2026 Masahiko G. Yamada. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0.

This informed maintenance study follows the fixed access decision in
[Issue #75](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/75). The context and four
first sources were saved before checking and before changing the lexer.
No external model was invoked. The session binds unchanged source/manifest
bytes and eight actual CLI observations, captured separately before/after.

Three receiver forms (quantum, mixed product and ordinary) remain parse
refusals at the same original dot. Their explanations now state the unsupported
field/method form and condition explicit-access advice on quantum use; they do
not claim to know the receiver type. The explicit-call control succeeds with
identical complete stdout/stderr. The observations check source acceptance,
not a probability distribution or a general source-preservation theorem.

No method syntax, receiver coercion, access inference, native rule or new
constitutional guarantee was added. Ordinary calls and range tokenization
remain unchanged. Separate Rust regressions check Unicode/CRLF locations,
both public source paths, missing-checker text/JSON refusals and bounded
ordinary/quantum positive outcomes. Hashes bind the observed executable bytes;
they do not attest its build or replace the independent acceptance boundary.
